improves reliability through two distinct channels: (1) it externalizes the expert's tacit cue selection into an explicit, repeatable procedure, reducing variance from attention lapses and mood; (2) the panel's aggregate judgment averages over independent, idiosyncratic errors of individual non-experts. The net gain over a single expert is the residual after subtracting the loss from non-expert cue-interpretation error. Within a single evaluation, a genuine reliability gain is distinguished from mere checklist compliance by examining whether panel members can correctly justify their checklist-driven answers on held-out items where the checklist is deliberately altered or where cues are masked\u2014if accuracy collapses on altered-checklist items but not on standard ones, the panel was merely following the checklist's surface pattern without understanding the cues.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
